proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 8.1 (pp. 173-174), displays (1)-(8), in the form of the parent proof's Steps 1-4. Errata/notation: the printed hypothesis Θⁿ(μ_T, x) > 0 is the upper density Θ*ⁿ (as used in (1)-(3)); the ‘Structure Theorem 3.8 of Ch. 3’ of the preamble of §8 is used through Theorem 3.6 and Lemma 3.2 of Ch. 3; the measure μ of the hypothesis plays the role of μ_T. The printed proof sets M := {x ∈ U : Θ*ⁿ(μ_T, x) > 0}; here M is first replaced by a Borel set B₀ ⊆ {Θ*ⁿ(μ, ·) > 0} that carries μ, and the Radon-Nikodym theorem is used in its abstract σ-finite form (the form recalled before Simon Ch. 1, 3.24), since Hⁿ⌞B₀ need not be Radon. Hⁿ = μHE[n]; D(x) := Θ*ⁿ(μ, x).

1. Preliminaries. Let W_q (q ∈ ℕ) be open sets ⊂⊂ U with W_q ↑ and ⋃_q W_q = U (exhaustion of the σ-compact open set U; every compact K ⊆ U lies in some W_q). By IsMassMeasure, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0 and μ(W_q) = M_{W_q}(T) < ∞; so μ is σ-finite and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. By the sibling mass_measure_abs_continuous, μ ≪ Hⁿ (for all sets).

2. A Borel carrier. The set Z′ := {x : ¬(D(x) > 0)} is μ-null by hypothesis; let Z ⊇ Z′ be a Borel μ-null set (a measurable hull) and B₀ := U∖Z. Then B₀ is Borel, B₀ ⊆ U ∩ {D > 0}, and μ(ℝ^P∖B₀) ≤ μ(ℝ^P∖U) + μ(Z) = 0.

3. σ-finiteness (printed (1)). For j, q ≥ 1 let A_{j,q} := B₀ ∩ W_q ∩ {D ≥ 1/j}. By the sibling density_comparison with V := W_q, A := A_{j,q} and t := 1/j, (1/j) Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) ≤ μ(W_q) < ∞, i.e. Hⁿ(A_{j,q}) ≤ j M_{W_q}(T) < ∞. Every x ∈ B₀ lies in some W_q and has D(x) > 0, hence D(x) ≥ 1/j for some j; so B₀ = ⋃_{j,q} A_{j,q} is a countable union of sets of finite Hⁿ-measure.

4. Rectifiability (printed (6), (7)). By Lemma 3.2 of Ch. 3 in its Borel form (SimonGMT measurable_rectifiable_purelyUnrectifiable_decomposition, applied to the Borel set B₀ and the cover of step 3), B₀ = R ∪ P′ with R Borel and countably n-rectifiable and P′ Hⁿ-measurable and purely n-unrectifiable. Since P′ ⊆ B₀ ⊆ ⋃ A_{j,q}, the sibling structure_projection gives a linear isometry Q with Lⁿ(p_α(Q(P′))) = 0 for all α ∈ I(n,P). As P′ is Hⁿ-measurable, P′ = B ∪ N with B ⊆ P′ Borel and Hⁿ(N) = 0. Then μ(N) = 0 because μ ≪ Hⁿ; and since Lⁿ(p_α(Q(B))) ≤ Lⁿ(p_α(Q(P′))) = 0 for all α, the sibling projection_null gives μ(B) = 0 (this is the use of Remark 2.37(2) in the printed proof). So μ(P′) = 0 (outer measure).
 Now fix j, q and ε > 0. μ⌞W_q is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence outer regular (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15(1)); since (μ⌞W_q)(P′ ∩ W_q) ≤ μ(P′) = 0, there is an open O ⊇ P′ ∩ W_q with μ(O ∩ W_q) < ε. The open set V := O ∩ W_q contains P′ ∩ A_{j,q}, on which D ≥ 1/j, so density_comparison gives (1/j) Hⁿ(P′ ∩ A_{j,q}) ≤ μ(V) < ε. Hence Hⁿ(P′ ∩ A_{j,q}) = 0 for all j, q, and Hⁿ(P′) = 0 because P′ ⊆ ⋃_{j,q} A_{j,q} (printed (6): Hⁿ(P) = 0 for every purely unrectifiable P ⊆ M). Therefore B₀ = R ∪ P′ is countably n-rectifiable (P′ is countably n-rectifiable, being Hⁿ-null, and a union of two countably rectifiable sets is countably rectifiable), and μ = μ⌞B₀ (printed (7)).

5. Radon-Nikodym (printed (8)). Let λ := Hⁿ⌞B₀. λ is σ-finite by step 3 (SimonGMT sigmaFinite_restrict_of_hausdorff_finite_cover), μ is σ-finite (step 1), and μ ≪ λ: if λ(S) = 0 for a Borel S then Hⁿ(S ∩ B₀) = 0, so μ(S ∩ B₀) = 0 (μ ≪ Hⁿ), and μ(S∖B₀) ≤ μ(ℝ^P∖B₀) = 0. By the Radon-Nikodym theorem (Mathlib Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq and Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top) there is a Borel h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] with μ = λ.withDensity(h), i.e. μ(S) = ∫_{S∩B₀} h dHⁿ for Borel S, and h < ∞ λ-a.e.

6. Positive real density. Let M := B₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} (Borel, M ⊆ B₀ ⊆ U, countably n-rectifiable as a subset of B₀) and θ := h.toReal (Borel and real-valued; θ = h ∈ (0, ∞) on M, so θ > 0 on M). For Borel S, μ(S) = ∫_{S∩B₀} h dHⁿ = ∫_{S∩M} h dHⁿ + ∫_{S∩B₀∩{h=0}} h dHⁿ + ∫_{S∩B₀∩{h=∞}} h dHⁿ = ∫_{S∩M} ofReal(θ) dHⁿ, because the second integrand vanishes, the third domain is λ-null, and ofReal(h.toReal) = h on M. Thus μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ).

7. Local integrability. For compact K ⊆ U choose q with K ⊆ W_q; then ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ = μ(M ∩ K) ≤ μ(W_q) = M_{W_q}(T) < ∞, and θ ≥ 0 is Borel, so θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K.

8. Summary. M ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ is Borel, positive on M and integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, and μ = θHⁿ⌞M. No dimension assumption is used: if P < n then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^P, μ = 0 by μ ≪ Hⁿ, and the argument above applies verbatim (M is then Hⁿ-null and both sides of μ = θHⁿ⌞M vanish). ∎
key_steps: Exhaust U by W_q ⊂⊂ U: μ(W_q) = M_{W_q}(T) < ∞, μ is σ-finite, and μ ≪ Hⁿ by mass_measure_abs_continuous.
Choose a Borel carrier B₀ ⊆ U ∩ {Θ*ⁿ(μ) > 0} with μ(ℝ^P∖B₀) = 0.
density_comparison: Hⁿ(B₀ ∩ W_q ∩ {Θ*ⁿ(μ) ≥ 1/j}) ≤ jμ(W_q), so B₀ is Hⁿ-σ-finite (printed (1)).

Lemma 3.2: B₀ = R ∪ P′; structure_projection, projection_null and absolute continuity give μ(P′) = 0; outer regularity and density_comparison give Hⁿ(P′) = 0, so B₀ is countably rectifiable (printed (6),(7)).
Radon-Nikodym for μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞B₀ (σ-finite) gives μ = hHⁿ⌞B₀ (printed (8)).
M := B₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} and θ := h.toReal give μ = θHⁿ⌞M with θ > 0 on M and locally integrable.
